documents.title: Colonoscopy timing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: GI wants to do the colonoscopy I skipped last summer while I was away. They have February 10. Is it OK to do that so soon after everything in the fall?

documents.title: RE: Colonoscopy timing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, your December counts were recovering well and it's due. Go ahead with the 10th.

events.reason: Surveillance colonoscopy, PSC with ulcerative colitis

reports.text: Random biopsies, four colonic segments and rectum: colonic mucosa with features of chronic, inactive colitis. No active inflammation. No dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Chronic inactive colitis. Negative for dysplasia.

documents.title: Surveillance Colonoscopy and PSC Review
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology and hepatology group. 02/10/2026.

Overdue surveillance (deferred during his deployment and autumn illness). Interval visceral leishmaniasis treated with liposomal amphotericin in October; histoplasmosis treated last spring.
Colonoscopy: complete to the ileum; healed mucosa throughout, no polyps or raised lesions. Segmental random biopsies show inactive colitis, no dysplasia.
PSC: MRCP in January stable compared with 2024, no dominant stricture or mass. CA 19-9 normal. Liver enzymes at his baseline on your last panel.
Meds: mesalamine 4.8 g daily, ursodiol 300 mg three times daily. NKDA.
Plan: unchanged. Colonoscopy and MRCP again in a year.

documents.title: Prior authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual PA for mesalamine DR 1.2 g due again with the student plan. Submitted with the 2/2026 GI letter. Approved same day through 2/2027.

events.reason: Visceral leishmaniasis, end of relapse surveillance

documents.title: Infectious Disease Follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outside infectious disease clinic. Visit 04/14/2026.

Six months after liposomal amphotericin B for visceral leishmaniasis. No fevers, sweats or weight loss. Back to full activity and Reserve drills.
Exam: no hepatosplenomegaly. Right forearm scar healed and stable.
CBC: hemoglobin 13.4, white count and platelets normal.

Assessment: visceral leishmaniasis, cured, without relapse. Prior histoplasmosis without recurrence.
Plan: discharged from routine ID follow-up. Relapse can occur late, particularly with future immunosuppression; please re-refer for fever, cytopenias or an enlarging spleen, and let us know before any rituximab or steroids.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
30M yearly exam, first since early 2024 (missed the 2025 one, then the spring histoplasmosis and the fall leishmaniasis).

Problem list reviewed: PSC on ursodiol; extensive UC in remission on mesalamine (surveillance colonoscopy 2/2026 without dysplasia); pemphigus vulgaris in remission off therapy since 2023; anemia, now nearly resolved (Hb 13.4 in April); histoplasmosis 2025, resolved; visceral leishmaniasis 2025, cured per ID in April.
Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g x4 daily, ursodiol 300 mg TID. NKDA.

Interval: feels well. Defending his dissertation in the fall. Reserve drills resumed; no deployment planned. Alcohol rare. No tobacco.

Exam: vitals as charted. Anicteric. Mouth clear. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Right forearm well-healed flat scar. Skin otherwise clear.
PHQ-9 2, AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
- PSC/UC stable; CMP and UA today, LFT/CBC again in August.
- Pemphigus in remission. ID asks to be told before any future rituximab or steroids; noted at top of the problem list.
- Vaccines: flu and COVID in the fall; PCV20 done 2023.
RTC September.
